verifiedAgainst.note: OBS has no default global hotkeys (every frontend hotkey is registered without a binding, S6), so the pack's real verbs are obs-websocket 5.x requests (S1) served by a planned Prism Control 'obs' module. The only default keys are main-window menu/preview shortcuts (S4, S6, S7), confirmed as strings in the local obs64.exe (S11). Request names were checked against the generated protocol doc on master; master adds canvas fields (5.7.0) that 5.5.5 doesn't have.

userBindings.summary: OBS ships no global hotkeys; users bind them in Settings > Hotkeys. Frontend hotkeys (stream, record, replay, studio mode, screenshot…) are saved per profile in basic.ini [Hotkeys] as one JSON value per hotkey name. Per-source hotkeys (scene switch, mute/unmute, push-to-talk, show/hide a scene item) are saved inside the scene collection JSON under each source's 'hotkeys' object. Prism reads them only to press the user's own key as a fallback when the websocket isn't connected.

locations.note: [Hotkeys] section. Value = JSON with newlines escaped as \n (libobs config-file). Absent here: OBS has never run for this user.

sources[].hotkeys (OBSBasic.SelectScene on scene sources, libobs.mute / libobs.unmute / libobs.push-to-talk / libobs.push-to-mute on audio sources, libobs.show_scene_item.<item> / libobs.hide_scene_item.<item> on scenes); global audio in DesktopAudioDevice1..2 / AuxAudioDevice1..4 objects with their own 'hotkeys'.

OBS 31+: [General] HotkeyFocusType (default NeverDisableHotkeys = hotkeys work even when OBS isn't focused) and [Basic] Profile / SceneCollection (which files above are active). OBS 30 and older keep these in global.ini.

obs-websocket server settings (ServerEnabled default false, ServerPort default 4455, AuthRequired default true, a generated ServerPassword). NEVER read or copy the password: Prism asks the user to paste it in the PI and stores it with DPAPI.
Portable mode (portable_mode.txt next to the install, or --portable): the same tree lives under the install folder.

userBindings.entryShape: basic.ini: '<hotkeyName>=<json>' under [Hotkeys], e.g. OBSBasic.StartStreaming; the JSON is {"bindings":[{"key":"OBS_KEY_*","shift"?:bool,"control"?:bool,"alt"?:bool,"command"?:bool}, …]} (several bindings allowed; an empty array = unbound). The replay buffer is the exception: key 'ReplayBuffer' holds {"ReplayBuffer.Save":[bindings]}. Scene collection: sources[i].hotkeys = {"<hotkeyName>": [bindings]}. The action id is the hotkey name, not the websocket request, so Prism joins through the table in the notes file (StartStream <- OBSBasic.StartStreaming, ToggleRecord <- OBSBasic.StartRecording/StopRecording, SaveReplayBuffer <- ReplayBuffer.Save, TriggerStudioModeTransition <- OBSBasic.Transition, SetCurrentProgramScene <- the scene's OBSBasic.SelectScene, ToggleInputMute <- libobs.mute/unmute …).
userBindings.keyNameMap: OBS_KEY_A..OBS_KEY_Z -> A..Z; OBS_KEY_0..9 -> 0..9; OBS_KEY_F1..F24 -> F1..F24; OBS_KEY_NUM0..NUM9 -> Numpad0..9; OBS_KEY_NUMPLUS/NUMMINUS/NUMASTERISK/NUMSLASH/NUMPERIOD -> NumpadAdd/NumpadSubtract/NumpadMultiply/NumpadDivide/NumpadDecimal; OBS_KEY_RETURN -> Enter, OBS_KEY_ESCAPE -> Esc, OBS_KEY_SPACE, OBS_KEY_TAB, OBS_KEY_BACKSPACE, OBS_KEY_INSERT, OBS_KEY_DELETE, OBS_KEY_HOME, OBS_KEY_END, OBS_KEY_PAGEUP, OBS_KEY_PAGEDOWN, OBS_KEY_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT, OBS_KEY_PRINT -> PrintScreen, OBS_KEY_SCROLLLOCK, OBS_KEY_PAUSE map by name. On Windows the OEM keys are: OBS_KEY_PLUS -> Equal (VK_OEM_PLUS), OBS_KEY_MINUS -> Minus, OBS_KEY_COMMA, OBS_KEY_PERIOD, OBS_KEY_SLASH, OBS_KEY_SEMICOLON, OBS_KEY_APOSTROPHE -> Quote, OBS_KEY_BRACKETLEFT/BRACKETRIGHT, OBS_KEY_BACKSLASH, OBS_KEY_ASCIITILDE -> Backquote (VK_OEM_3), OBS_KEY_BACKSLASH_RT102 -> IntlBackslash. Modifiers: control -> Ctrl, alt -> Alt, shift -> Shift (command is macOS). OBS_KEY_MOUSE1..29 are mouse buttons: no chord, keep the verb on its module binding. Media keys (OBS_KEY_VK_MEDIA_*) -> MediaPlayPause etc.
userBindings.readMode: Read-only. Read user.ini for the active profile and scene collection, parse basic.ini [Hotkeys] (unescape \n, then JSON) and the collection JSON's hotkeys, watch both files (OBS rewrites them on settings save and on exit). Never open plugin_config/obs-websocket/config.json. A user hotkey is only a fallback: with the websocket connected, the request is always used because it reports true state.
userBindings.verify: Once OBS has been run and a hotkey set, confirm the basic.ini line format on this PC (the example is fictional, built from the source).

layouts.rationale: Go live / record / replay on top, scenes in the middle with the two mute keys, mode and capture keys at the bottom; volume and scene dials, health readouts on the screen.
Same places as offline so muscle memory holds: the stream key becomes END STREAM (hold), scenes and mutes stay put, and the bottom row trades setup keys for on-air source toggles.
Recording tools replace replay on the top row (pause next to stop), chapter and split take the free slots; the screen swaps stream health for record time and free disk.
Scene keys load the preview, TAKE sits top-right where the hand rests, Cut/Fade pick the transition; the screen shows the queued preview scene and the transition length.
Outputs and mic mute on top, three scenes and desktop mute below; each dial's strip segment shows its own value.
Same keys as offline with END STREAM in the stream slot; while live the right half of the strip shows stream time and dropped frames (the picked scene glows on its key).
TAKE next to the stream key, scenes load the preview; the strip shows the queued scene and transition length over their dials.

conflicts: Redo: the KB (S4) lists only Ctrl-Shift-Z; 31.0.2 (S6) also binds Ctrl+Y.
Quit: the KB (S4) lists Ctrl-Q for Windows/Linux; 31.0.2 (S6) sets Ctrl+Q only on Linux. Not used in the pack.
The protocol doc (S1) is generated from master and shows canvasUuid fields (added 5.7.0); the bundled 5.5.5 (S11) predates them, so the module must not send canvas fields to 5.5.x.
gaps: Everything in the obs.* namespace is planned: the Prism Control obs module (websocket client, auth via a user-pasted password, reconnect, InputVolumeMeters decimation) doesn't exist yet.

The pack is matched by foreground process, but streamers mostly need these controls while a game is in front. The engine needs a way to keep an 'app running / module connected' pack available in the background or as a pinned overlay page.
Join key: verbs use the websocket request name as appAction, while user hotkeys are keyed by OBS hotkey names; the mapping lives in userBindings.entryShape and the notes file, not in a field.
Not tested against a running OBS: OBS has never been launched here and websocket is off by default.
SplitRecordFile preconditions and localized transition names are unverified.
notes: OBS has no default global hotkeys. The only built-in keys are main-window shortcuts (transform, order, nudge, undo/redo, F2 rename, Del remove, F11 fullscreen interface); they need OBS focused, and the nudge keys need the preview focused.
OBS hotkeys are global by default (HotkeyFocusType NeverDisableHotkeys), so the user's own hotkeys work as a fallback even with a game in front.
Long-form notes, the verb-to-request table and the hotkey-name join table: packs/notes/obs-studio.md.
